t3.descripcion:
🔹 EXPRESSIONS WITH DAR (expressions with dar):

• dar la hora = to tell the time
• dar las gracias = to thank
• dar un paseo = to take a walk
• dar vergüenza = to be embarrassing
• dar miedo = to be scary
• dar igual = to not matter
• dar un beso = to give a kiss
• dar un abrazo = to give a hug
• dar la lata = to be annoying
• dar en el clavo = to hit the nail on the head

🔹 EXPRESSIONS WITH ECHAR (expressions with echar):

• echar de menos = to miss (someone/something)
• echar un vistazo = to take a look
• echar la culpa = to blame
• echar una mano = to lend a hand
• echarse a reír = to burst out laughing
• echarse a llorar = to burst into tears
• echar un ojo = to keep an eye on
• echar gasolina = to put gasoline
• echar una siesta = to take a nap

📌 EXAMPLES:
• Te echo de menos.
• Échale un vistazo a este documento.
• No me eches la culpa.

❌ NOTE:
"Echar de menos" is a very common expression that has no literal equivalent in English. It means "extrañar".
ejemplos: Me da vergüenza hablar en público.
Le echan de menos en su país.

t4.descripcion:
🔹 EXPRESSIONS WITH "ESTAR":
• estar de buen humor = to be in a good mood
• estar de mal humor = to be in a bad mood
• estar de vacaciones = to be on vacation
• estar de moda = to be in fashion
• estar al tanto = to be up to date
• estar harto = to be fed up
• estar de acuerdo = to agree

🔹 EXPRESSIONS WITH "PONERSE":
• ponerse nervioso = to get nervous
• ponerse contento = to get happy
• ponerse triste = to get sad
• ponerse furioso = to get furious
• ponerse rojo = to blush
• ponerse las pilas = to get one's act together

🔹 EXPRESSIONS WITH "LLEVAR":
• llevar tiempo = to take time
• llevar la contraria = to disagree
• llevar bien/mal = to get along well/badly
• llevar a cabo = to carry out

🔹 EXPRESSIONS WITH "QUEDARSE":
• quedarse dormido = to fall asleep
• quedarse sin palabras = to be speechless
• quedarse con la boca abierta = to be astonished
• quedarse en blanco = to draw a blank

📌 EXAMPLES:
• Hoy estoy de buen humor.
• Me puse nervioso antes del examen.
• Me quedé sin palabras cuando lo vi.
• Llevo tiempo aprendiendo español.

t1.descripcion:
Very common expressions with TENER:

🔹 PHYSICAL STATES AND EMOTIONS:
• tener hambre = to be hungry
• tener sed = to be thirsty
• tener sueño = to be sleepy
• tener calor = to be hot
• tener frío = to be cold
• tener prisa = to be in a hurry
• tener suerte = to be lucky
• tener cuidado = to be careful
• tener razón = to be right
• tener miedo = to be afraid
• tener vergüenza = to be embarrassed / ashamed
• tener esperanza = to have hope
• tener confianza = to have confidence

🔹 WISHES AND FEELINGS:
• tener ganas de = to feel like (doing something)
• tener celos = to be jealous
• tener envidia = to be envious
• tener paciencia = to have patience

🔹 RELATIONSHIPS:
• tener éxito = to be successful
• tener problemas = to have problems
• tener la culpa = to be guilty / to blame

📌 EXAMPLES:
• Tengo mucha hambre.
• ¡Ten cuidado con el coche!
• Tienes razón, lo siento.
• Tengo ganas de comer pizza.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE:
Do not use "ser" or "estar" to express hunger, thirst, etc. Always use "tener".

t2.descripcion:
🔹 VERY COMMON IDIOMATIC EXPRESSIONS:

• estar hecho polvo = to be exhausted
• ser pan comido = to be a piece of cake
• costar un ojo de la cara = to cost an arm and a leg
• no tener ni idea = to have no idea
• dar igual = to not care / to be indifferent
• estar como una cabra = to be crazy
• ser uña y carne = to be inseparable (thick as thieves)
• no hay tu tía = there's no way
• tomar el pelo = to pull someone's leg
• estar en las nubes = to be daydreaming / distracted
• ponerse las pilas = to get one's act together / to step up
• ir al grano = to get to the point
• matar el tiempo = to kill time
• echar una mano = to lend a hand
• estar hasta las narices = to be fed up

🔹 EXAMPLES:
• Estoy hecho polvo después del trabajo.
• Este examen será pan comido.
• Este coche cuesta un ojo de la cara.

📌 DETAILED MEANINGS:
• estar hecho polvo: muy cansado
• ser pan comido: muy fácil
• costar un ojo de la cara: muy caro
• no tener ni idea: no saber nada
• dar igual: no importar
• estar como una cabra: estar loco
• ser uña y carne: ser inseparables
• tomar el pelo: bromear, engañar
• estar en las nubes: distraído
• ponerse las pilas: espabilarse, activarse
• ir al grano: decir lo esencial
ejemplos: No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.
Me da igual qué película veamos.
Son uña y carne, siempre juntos.

dict.昨天对玛尔塔来说是疯狂的一天。她起晚了，因为看剧看得睡着了。当她看表时，发现自己: Yesterday was a crazy day for Marta. She got up late because she fell asleep watching a series. When she looked at the clock, she realized she was in a big hurry: she was going to be late for work! She rushed out without breakfast, so by around ten in the morning she was already hungry and thirsty. At the office, her boss asked her to do an urgent report, but she had no idea where to start. To make matters worse, a colleague blamed her for a mistake she didn't make. Marta was in a bad mood and exhausted. However, she decided to pull herself together and get straight to the point. In the end, she finished the report on time and her boss agreed she was right. But when she got home and saw that the cat had scratched the sofa, she was speechless. What a terrible day!
dict.玛尔塔为什么赶时间？: Why is Marta in a hurry?
dict.文中提到她起晚了，因为看剧睡着了，发现上班要迟到，所以赶时间。: The text mentions she got up late because she fell asleep watching a series, realized she was going to be late for work, so she was in a hurry.
dict.玛尔塔'no tenía ni idea'（一无所知）怎么开始报告是什么意思？: What does it mean that Marta 'no tenía ni idea' (had no idea) how to start the report?

dict.文中说'Marcia estaba de mal humor y hecha p: The text says 'Marcia estaba de mal humor y hecha polvo', i.e., in a bad mood and exhausted.

dict.西班牙与拉丁美洲的口语表达: Colloquial expressions in Spain and Latin America
dict.在西班牙语世界，习语表达因国家而异。例如，在西班牙很常说'estar hecho: In the Spanish-speaking world, idiomatic expressions vary by country. For example, in Spain it's very common to say 'estar hecho polvo' to mean extreme fatigue, while in Mexico 'estar hasta el tope' or 'estar muerto' are more common. Another interesting difference: in Spain they say 'coger el metro' (take the subway), but in Argentina they tend to say 'tomar el subte'. Also, expressions like 'ser pan comido' are understood almost everywhere, but others are regional. Learning these variants helps you speak more naturally and avoid misunderstandings.
dict.在中国，方言中的习语也差异很大，比如北方人说“累成狗”，南方人可能说“累趴了”。: In China, idioms in dialects also vary greatly; for example, northerners say “累成狗” (dog-tired), while southerners might say “累趴了” (worn out). Spanish also has regional differences, so pay attention to context when learning.
dict.此句本身正确，但中国学生常混淆'tener prisa'（赶时间）和'estar: This sentence is correct in itself, but Chinese students often confuse 'tener prisa' (be in a hurry) and 'estar preocupado' (worry); note that 'tener prisa' is not “anxious” but “pressed for time”.
dict.描述过去的状态应用未完成时'estaba'，而不是现在时'estoy'。中国学生: To describe a past state, use the imperfect 'estaba', not the present 'estoy'. Chinese students often ignore tense agreement.
dict.此句正确，但学生常误用'ser'和'estar'：'ser pan comido: This sentence is correct, but students often misuse 'ser' and 'estar': 'ser pan comido' is a fixed expression and cannot use 'estar'.
dict.后接从句时需用虚拟式，中国学生常忽略虚拟式。: When followed by a clause, the subjunctive is required; Chinese students often ignore the subjunctive.
dict.直接接名词，不加介词'a'（除非是人）。中国学生易受母语影响加'a'。: Directly followed by a noun, without the preposition 'a' (unless it's a person). Chinese students are easily influenced by their native language and add 'a'.
